title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 772-774 of the 'suite à la Longue Marche'): X is a topological surface, U is X minus a finite set of points, and x is one of the removed points. D_x^* = D^*_{X,x} is the 'germe résiduel' of X at x, i.e. the germ of punctured neighbourhoods of x, treated as a kind of pro-space or topos. Its category of coverings Rev(D_x^*) is Galois with cyclic group T_x (topologically Z, profinitely Ẑ). The previous page built the local-monodromy homomorphism T_x -> π = π_1(U, Ũ). It depends on choosing a universal covering D_x^{*~} of D_x^* together with a lift into Ũ, and is well defined only up to inner automorphism, as the 'exterior' homomorphism π_1(D_x^*) -> π_1(U).

Section C, begun at the bottom of p.773 and continued here, gives a convenient way to rigidify this choice by a germ of arc leaving x.
- Let I = [0,1] and let [I] be the residual germ of I at 0, i.e. the germ of ]0,ε].
- [I] is a 1-connected germ (indeed contractible), so Rev([I]) ≃ (Ens).
- A germ of arc of X issuing from x is a morphism of germs γ: [I] -> germ rés_x(X) = D_x^* (eq. 66).
- Concretely, it is a continuous map φ: [0,ε] -> X with φ(0) = x and φ(t) ≠ x for t in ]0,ε] (eqs. 67-68).
- Pulling coverings back along γ gives a fibre functor Rev(D_x^*) -> Rev([I]) ≃ (Ens) (eq. 69).

The next page uses this fibre functor:
- It defines the universal covering D_x^{*~} = Rev univ(D_x^*, ([I], φ)).
- It gets a factorisation [I] -> D_x^{*~} -> D_x^* -> U, hence a canonical isomorphism Rev univ(U, D_x^{*~}) ≃ Rev univ(U, [I]).
- So the arc germ, viewed as a base point of U, yields a genuine homomorphism K_x: T_x -> π_1(U, [I]), not just a conjugacy class.
- Section D then specialises to differentiable arcs, i.e. towards base points given by tangent directions at x.

The diagonal marginal note (only partly legible) muses that instead of passing through germs [I] of neighbourhoods of 0 in [0,1], it might be better to define the fibre functors otherwise. Fragments read 'germes', 'Weil', 'systèmes progressifs' (pro-systems).

In modern terms, this is the topological precursor of tangential base points: the 'base point at a puncture' that makes the inertia map T_x -> π_1(U) canonical rather than defined up to conjugacy.
errors: No mathematical error. Rev([I]) ≃ Ens holds because every germ of ]0,ε] is contractible; the fibre does not depend on ε (shrinking ε gives canonical bijections).

Implicit point: two arc germs give isomorphic fibre functors, but the isomorphism is not canonical. Arc germs with values in D_x^* fall into homotopy classes that form a T_x-torsor (winding), so a merely continuous arc pins down the base point only up to the choice of class. This is why the differentiable refinement of the next page (tangent direction) is needed to make the choice 'canonical up to contractible choice'. The page does not state this explicitly.

ideas.what: Residual germ D_x^* (punctured-neighbourhood germ) of a space at a point, as an object with its own covering category Rev(D_x^*), Galois with group T_x
ideas.modern_name: punctured neighbourhood / local fundamental group at a puncture (deleted neighbourhood pro-space; 'link' at infinity)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (local monodromy); the germ/topos formulation is Grothendieck's (SGA1, SGA2 local π_1)
ideas.where_published: SGA 1 XIII and SGA 2 (local fundamental groups in the algebraic setting); this topological germ version is unsure

ideas.what: Germs of arcs [I] -> D_x^* as base points (fibre functors) on Rev(D_x^*) and on Rev(U), rigidifying the inertia homomorphism T_x -> π_1(U, [I])
ideas.modern_name: tangential base points (topological version: base points 'at a puncture' given by germs of paths)
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Deligne, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points' (1989); Ihara and others in the profinite/GT setting
ideas.where_published: Possibly hinted at in Esquisse d'un programme / La Longue Marche (1981) in discussions of base points; unsure

ideas.what: Refinement to differentiable arc germs, i.e. base points given by tangent directions (announced in section D on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: tangential base point given by a tangent vector or direction

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently develops (likely early 1980s, in the Longue Marche continuation) the device of using germs of arcs leaving a puncture as base points. These make local inertia T_x -> π_1(U) an honest homomorphism, with a differentiable refinement that leads to tangential base points. This predates or parallels Deligne's 1989 tangential base points and is not credited to him in the literature.
missed.quote: germe d'arc de courbe [...] X issu de x, les morphismes [I] -> germ rés_x(X) = D_x^* [...] on peut utiliser cet arc pour définir un foncteur fibre sur D_x^*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority/genealogy point for tangential base points, central in Grothendieck-Teichmüller theory and in motivic fundamental groups. The 'residual germ' formalism also gives a clean topos-theoretic framework for base points at infinity.

missed.claim: The marginal note proposes replacing interval germs [I] by some other fibre-functor construction, apparently via pro-systems ('systèmes progressifs'). This hints at defining base points at a puncture intrinsically as pro-objects or points of the residual-germ topos rather than via arcs.
missed.quote: Plutôt que de [prendre?] l'(Ens) par des germes [I] de voisinages de 0 dans [0,1], il vaudrait peut-être mieux définir les foncteurs fibres ... systèmes progressifs
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This relates to modern treatments of base points as points of the punctured-neighbourhood (or 'nearby cycles') topos, but it is too fragmentary to assess.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clear, early, unpublished formulation of tangential/arc-germ base points in Grothendieck's own residual-germ language, a notion usually credited to Deligne (1989). The mathematics itself is elementary, and Grothendieck's general awareness of base-point issues in the Longue Marche is known, so the surprise is moderate.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: 'on [appellera?]' reads as 'on appelle' (abbreviated '..'); the struck-out text is 'de' before 'X issu de x'.
Eq. (66) annotation above the right side reads 'D^*_{X,x}' (the transcription's 'D_{*,x}' variant is a misreading).
The parenthesis reads roughly '(X une surface au voisinage de x, donc Rev(D_x^*) galoisienne cyclique de groupe T_x)'; 'surface' is uncertain but consistent with context.
The marginal note is largely illegible; fragments 'germes', 'voisinages de 0 dans [0,1]', 'Weil', 'systèmes progressifs' are plausible but uncertain.
